messages:
anya: heads-up — trying to bring up gemma-7b-v2 (HF checkpoint -> our serving) on dedicated pool. generation is weird: extra punctuation and repeated tokens at start. suspect vocab/id shift or pos encoding mismatch. anyone seen this with qwen tokenizer + gemma weights?

ross: interesting. did you convert the tokenizer vocab.json or reuse our qwen vocab?

anya: reused qwen tokenizer for inference to match customer pipeline. example: encode('Hello') returns [320, 11] on Qwen, but model expects [321, 11] based on HF artifacts. logs: 
```
Tokenizer.encode('Hello') -> [320, 11]
Model.embedding[320][:5] -> [0.0123, -0.0032, 0.0045, ...]
Model.embedding[321][:5] -> [0.512, 0.47, -0.12, ...]
Decoded from model logits argmax for first token -> token id 321 -> 'ĠHello' but tokenizer maps 320 -> 'Hello'
```

mike: that smells like an off-by-one in the vocab mapping or a different BOS/SPECIAL token ordering. check tokenizer.special_tokens_map and vocab size mismatch (e.g., 50280 vs 50281).

anya: special_tokens_map looks identical, but vocab.json lengths differ: HF checkpoint vocab_size=50281, our qwen vocab_size=50280. also saw kv-cache misalignment in the traces — attention keys showing shifted positions.

sam: could be positional encoding style mismatch — gemma uses rotary with a particular base/freq schedule. if we accidentally applied ALiBi or different rotary scaling at compile time, kv alignment + token id mismatch would both show up. did you load model config rotary_* params?

anya: config snippet: 
```json
{"rotary_pct": 0.25, "rotary_dim": 64, "rotary_base": 10000}
```
but our runtime defaults to rotary_base=4096 when not set. i think converter dropped the field.

ross: ok that explains rotary scale issues, but not vocab id shift. converter might have collapsed an explicit <pad> token. Two action items: 1) align vocab.json sizes, 2) ensure rotary params from config are passed through the compiler.

eval-bot: automated eval: comparing hf-ref vs serving-converted on eval-small: perplexity +12.3%, exact-match on whitespace-sensitive tokens down 7.8%. top-1 token mismatch frequent at sequence start.

mike: quick repro: run tokenizer.encode and then tokenizer.convert_ids_to_tokens on the checkpoint vocab and on our serving vocab, diff them. i can drop a script.

anya: dropping repro now. script output: 
```
# diff snippet
- 320: "Hello"
+ 320: "ĠHello"
- 321: "ĠHello"
+ 321: "Hello"
```
so HF has leading-space variant at different id.

sam: so two orthogonal fixes: map ids (vocab remap table) OR re-export tokenizer from HF to match model. remap is faster but risky. preferred: re-export tokenizer and keep converter strict.

ross: also check quantization packing pass — if we quantized embeddings and applied row-shift packing with an assumption on padding token id, offsets could move. any quant pass logs?

anya: quant run used our standard int8 pipeline. logs show "embedding_pack_offset = 1" line which triggered me.

mike: yeah that offset should be 0 for this model. looks like our quant packing auto-detected a pad token and inserted a dummy row. bad.

deploy-bot: canary deploy 2026-03-20T09:12:15Z: gemma-7b-v2-converted -> pool-a (10%)

anya: plan: rollback canary, re-export tokenizer from HF checkpoint (preserve special tokens order), re-run converter ensuring rotary_base copied, rerun quant with embedding_pack_offset=0, then run eval-bot harness. will ping here when each step done.

ross: :thumbsup: let me know if you want me to handle remap script or we prefer full re-export.

anya: i'll try re-export first. if that fails i'll ask for remap script. tagging @sam in case of rotary compiler changes. :thinking: 

sam: i'll audit the converter to ensure rotary params are preserved and add a CI check for vocab_size equality.

eval-bot: queued eval job 17402 for post-fix comparison.

mike: logging the root cause as "tokenizer-conversion/vocab-offset + rotary-param-drop -> generation regressions". short postmortem draft after fix.

anya: thanks team — updating status in the onboarding doc and will paste final diffs here.
